annotation_description: Playing Verdant Catacombs (fetches Swamp or Forest) before Windswept Heath (fetches Forest or Plains) wastes the more versatile fetch. In this GB deck, Windswept Heath can fetch a Forest for Young Wolf just as well, while saving Verdant Catacombs for later when a Swamp might be needed for black spells like Thoughtseize or Fatal Push.

Green Sun's Zenith for X=0 could search for Dryad Arbor (a common inclusion in Modern GSZ decks) to ramp, or at minimum shuffles itself back into the library for future use. However, even without Dryad Arbor in the deck, GSZ for X=0 fetches any green creature with mana value 0. Young Wolf is a key piece for the Agatha's Soul Cauldron combo (providing undying), so playing it directly is defensible. That said, if the deck runs Dryad Arbor, GSZ for X=0 would have been strictly better here as it ramps while preserving Young Wolf in hand for a later combo turn with Cauldron. The reasoning explicitly dismissed GSZ for X=0 without considering what it could find, suggesting a missed opportunity.

Gem25F Sarge passed the turn without using any of their available mana or abilities. They could have activated Windswept Heath to fetch a land (thinning their deck and enabling revolt for potential Fatal Push interactions, plus getting a Swamp or Forest), and then cast Malevolent Rumble or Dredger's Insight to fill the graveyard and develop their game plan. They had a Forest untapped and Windswept Heath available to sacrifice for another land, giving them 2 mana to work with for Malevolent Rumble, Dredger's Insight, or Agatha's Soul Cauldron. Instead they did nothing, wasting an entire turn's worth of mana.

message: Select a Forest or Plains card
annotation_description: Fetching a basic Forest instead of Overgrown Tomb means Sarge has no access to black mana this turn or next turn without playing Underground Mortuary (which enters tapped). The hand contains Agatha's Soul Cauldron (colorless, fine), Malevolent Rumble (1G, fine), Green Sun's Zenith (XG, fine), and Dredger's Insight (1G, fine) — but also Underground Mortuary which enters tapped. Getting Overgrown Tomb untapped (paying 2 life) would provide immediate black mana access for future turns, enabling cards like Emperor of Bones or Thoughtseize that might be drawn. With the graveyard already containing fetchlands (enabling revolt for Fatal Push if drawn), having black mana available is more flexible. The basic Forest provides no color fixing advantage over what's already available.

Discarding Spell Pierce over Archon of Cruelty is a significant mistake. The player has Steam Vents as their only land - they're unlikely to cast an 8-mana Archon of Cruelty naturally. Meanwhile, Spell Pierce is a 1-mana counterspell that could protect against the opponent's key plays or disrupt their gameplan. The player does have cards that could potentially reanimate or cheat Archon into play (Emperor of Bones can exile cards from graveyards and reanimate them), but Archon in hand isn't useful for that - it would need to be in the graveyard. Spell Pierce is immediately castable and relevant against noncreature spells the opponent might play. If they need to discard to hand size (going to 7), Archon of Cruelty is the clear discard since it's an 8-drop with no realistic path to being cast.

Failed to crack Verdant Catacombs first to get a 4th land, which would have allowed casting both Agatha's Soul Cauldron (2 mana) and Dredger's Insight (1G) in the same turn. Dredger's Insight mills 4 cards which could immediately provide creature card targets for the Cauldron's exile ability.

message: Select a Swamp or Forest card
annotation_description: Fetched Overgrown Tomb instead of basic Swamp when already having two Forests for green mana. The extra green from Overgrown Tomb is largely redundant, and paying 2 life to enter untapped (or having it enter tapped) is worse than a free untapped basic Swamp. With Underground Mortuary also in hand as another B/G source, the flexibility of Overgrown Tomb provides minimal value.

Player passed with available mana and a strong play available. Dredger's Insight could be cast using Overgrown Tomb ({G}) + sacrificing Eldrazi Spawn Token ({1}), which would mill 4 cards, potentially find a key piece, and fuel the graveyard strategy. The player's reasoning about Agatha's Soul Cauldron having no targets was also factually wrong (8 cards in their own graveyard), though none were creatures so the counter wouldn't trigger. Additionally, Underground Mortuary should have been played this turn since it enters tapped anyway.

Green Sun's Zenith for X=3 (using both Forests, Delighted Halfling, and Eldrazi Spawn sacrifice) could find a powerful 3-CMC green creature to put immediate pressure on an opponent with only 2 lands. Instead, cast Dredger's Insight which is a value play but doesn't advance the board meaningfully against a stumbling opponent.

The player is resolving Dredger's Insight's mill trigger, choosing which card to put into hand. Walking Ballista is a key combo piece with Agatha's Soul Cauldron already on the battlefield - the Cauldron can exile creature cards from graveyards and grant their activated abilities to creatures with +1/+1 counters. Walking Ballista's 'Remove a +1/+1 counter: deal 1 damage' ability combined with Cauldron is a well-known infinite combo enabler. Even without the combo, Walking Ballista is a flexible card that scales with mana. Badgermole Cub, while decent for mana acceleration, is far less impactful. The player should have taken Walking Ballista to hand - either to cast it or to have it available for the Cauldron combo. With Agatha's Soul Cauldron already in play, having Walking Ballista in hand (to potentially cast and use, or to get into graveyard for Cauldron to exile) is significantly more valuable than Badgermole Cub.

Discarded Fatal Push, which is cheap, live removal that could interact with the opponent's Soul Cauldron combo pieces (Young Wolf with +1/+1 counter, Delighted Halfling). Archon of Cruelty is an 8-mana card with only 2 lands in play and no realistic way to cheat it into play (Unearth only hits MV ≤3). Archon's only purpose in this hand is as Psychic Frog discard fuel, but any card serves that role equally well.

Casting Green Sun's Zenith for X=4 uses all available mana when Agatha's Soul Cauldron is on the battlefield with Walking Ballista in the graveyard. Activating Soul Cauldron to exile Walking Ballista (giving a creature with +1/+1 counters the Ballista's ping ability) plus casting Badgermole Cub from hand could develop the board and advance the combo plan more efficiently. Without knowing what 4-CMC green creature is being fetched, this may be suboptimal sequencing.

Gem25F Sarge declined to activate Agatha's Soul Cauldron, which is a free tap ability that exiles a card from a graveyard (there are targets in both graveyards) and potentially puts a +1/+1 counter on a creature if a creature card is exiled. The opponent's graveyard has Fatal Push and Unearth (both non-creatures) and Spell Pierce (non-creature), but Sarge's own graveyard contains Walking Ballista (a creature card). Exiling Walking Ballista with Agatha's Soul Cauldron would put a +1/+1 counter on a creature Sarge controls, AND give all creatures with +1/+1 counters the activated abilities of Walking Ballista (including the 'remove a +1/+1 counter to deal 1 damage' ability). This is a significant value engine that was passed up for no reason. The Cauldron is already untapped and ready to use.

With only 2 lands on turn 5, Archon of Cruelty (8 mana) is essentially uncastable from hand. Discarding it would be better since it could potentially be reanimated via Emperor of Bones (exile from graveyard, then put onto battlefield). Thoughtseize at 1 mana is immediately castable and can disrupt the opponent's plans, which is critical when this far behind on board.

Missed infinite damage combo. Agatha's Soul Cauldron can exile Walking Ballista from graveyard, putting a +1/+1 counter on Young Wolf. Young Wolf then has Walking Ballista's 'Remove a +1/+1 counter: deal 1 damage' ability. Remove the counter, Young Wolf becomes 1/1, ping for 1. Then remove another... actually Young Wolf dies as a 0/0 when counter is removed, undying triggers (no +1/+1 counters), returns with a +1/+1 counter, repeat for infinite damage = lethal.

chosen_display: Spymaster's Vault — {B}, {T}: Target creature you control connives X,... [Activate]
annotation_description: Activated Spymaster's Vault to connive X where X equals the number of creatures that died this turn, which is 0. This means the activation does absolutely nothing — draws 0 cards, discards 0 cards — while tapping the land and spending {B} for no benefit.

Gem25F Sarge declined to activate Agatha's Soul Cauldron's tap ability, which would exile a card from a graveyard (such as Walking Ballista from their own graveyard) and put a +1/+1 counter on a creature they control. This is a pure-upside activated ability that costs nothing but a tap. Exiling Walking Ballista with Agatha's Soul Cauldron is particularly powerful because it gives all creatures with +1/+1 counters the ability to remove counters to deal damage — a key combo piece in the Agatha's Soul Cauldron deck. The player also declined to cast the second copy of Agatha's Soul Cauldron, which while legendary (so they can't have two), they could have at least activated the one on the battlefield. The reasoning given was nonsensical frustration rather than strategic thinking.

Gem25F Sarge has Endurance (3/4) available to attack alongside Young Wolf, but only sends the Young Wolf. The opponent has only 14 life and an empty board (just two lands), so there's no risk of unfavorable blocks. Attacking with both Young Wolf and Endurance would deal 4 damage instead of 1, representing significant pressure. The Endurance has no summoning sickness issues (it's listed as an available attacker), and leaving it back serves no defensive purpose against an opponent with an empty board.

Walking Ballista is in the graveyard and Agatha's Soul Cauldron is on the battlefield untapped. Exiling Walking Ballista with the Cauldron would put a +1/+1 counter on a creature AND give that creature Walking Ballista's activated abilities (remove counter to deal 1 damage, pay {4} to add a counter). This is a powerful combo interaction that was available and apparently ignored.

message: Select card to discard (selected 0 of 2, min 2)
annotation_description: Discarding Psychic Frog is a significant mistake. Psychic Frog is a 2-mana creature that synergizes extremely well with the discard-heavy gameplan, can grow with +1/+1 counters by discarding cards, gains flying, and draws cards on combat damage. With only 2 lands in play (Steam Vents and Island), Llama4 Timmy needs cheap, impactful plays. Psychic Frog at UB is castable next turn with a Bloodstained Mire fetch. Meanwhile, Archon of Cruelty at 6BB is completely uncastable for many turns and could have been discarded instead - it's a reanimation target but there's no reanimation spell in hand or evident in the deck. Discarding Archon of Cruelty (as a potential future reanimation target that's dead in hand) alongside Emperor of Bones would have been better, keeping both Psychic Frogs as the primary game plan with 2 lands.

Gem25F Sarge had the infinite combo available: Activate Agatha's Soul Cauldron to exile Walking Ballista from graveyard, putting a +1/+1 counter on Young Wolf. Young Wolf then gains Walking Ballista's 'remove a +1/+1 counter: deal 1 damage' ability. Removing the counter kills Young Wolf, undying returns it with a +1/+1 counter, and the loop repeats for infinite damage — killing the opponent at 10 life.

Gem25F Sarge declined to activate Agatha's Soul Cauldron to exile Walking Ballista from a graveyard (Llama4 Timmy's graveyard has no Walking Ballista, but their own graveyard has one). Exiling Walking Ballista with Agatha's Soul Cauldron is a key combo piece - it gives all creatures with +1/+1 counters the ability to remove counters to deal damage, and Walking Ballista's activated abilities. With Young Wolf (which has undying and can get +1/+1 counters) on the battlefield, this creates a powerful synergy. The Walking Ballista is on the stack resolving, but there's also one in Sarge's own graveyard that could be exiled with the Cauldron. Declining this activation wastes a critical combo opportunity.

Gem25F Sarge declined to activate Agatha's Soul Cauldron to exile Walking Ballista from the opponent's graveyard. Walking Ballista is one of the most powerful cards to exile with Agatha's Soul Cauldron, as it gives all creatures with +1/+1 counters the ability to remove counters to deal 1 damage to any target. Young Wolf with undying gets a +1/+1 counter when it returns, and the Cauldron itself can put +1/+1 counters on creatures by exiling creature cards. Exiling Walking Ballista with the Cauldron would enable a powerful combo engine where any creature with a +1/+1 counter becomes a damage source. The player's reasoning was confused, claiming the activation wasn't relevant, but this is actually a key synergy in their deck.
